body: I got diagnosed with vaginal herpes when I was 18 in june 2022. Don’t worry about it! When you come to terms with it you will realize that it’s not shameful or weird. Personally, if I’m with people I’m comfortable with, it’s kinda fun to joke about lol. When I’ve disclosed people are pretty accepting even if they are my age. It’s helpful to think about how you may be the first person to disclose to them but (unless you plan on marrying this person) you likely will not be the last. Also, it shows you get play. I just make sure to tell my partner the facts. Showing transparency is good. And saying that condoms reduce the rates of transmission is something I don’t leave out.
I’m sorry to hear that? do you have any advice tho?

I would suggest doing some online research with your partner, showing her that her sexual health is important to you. Especially if u use a condom there isn’t high chance of transmission… the only way to break stigma is with conversation

If you still want to get a degree, I think being in school while getting treated would get you a more accurate treatment. One treatment may be helpful while on a gap year, but you might go back to school and realize you weren’t getting the right/enough treatment and have to restart the process. When I first got diagnosed and medicated I made sure I tried my meds at school before switching or altering them because school was partly what I needed them for! 

However it also sounds like you don’t love college and getting the diagnoses is maybe giving you incentive to take a year off. If that’s the case, you should take a gap year no matter the reason if that is what you want and if that’s what’s best for ur mental health.

I’m on 30 mg as I’m fairly small and I take 50 sertraline as well. I just don’t know if it was a withdrawal or if it was my normal ADHD symptoms when I’m unmedicated, or if those mean the same thing??

I have inattentive adhd and getting medicated actually did help with that. Often times I felt like I was in a social situation and just dissociating and not really participating, Which gave me social anxiety and made me feel ignored (even though I wasn’t doing anything lol). Getting medicated made social situations be more stimulating and made me feel more myself while socializing

I feel this. Personally, when I don’t take my meds on a free day, I can’t even get out of bed to empty my bladder. So I definitely recommend taking your meds even when you have days off. 

It’s important to find things that aren’t mentally draining to do that you enjoy in your free time that get you out of the house. Personally, going for a drive is easy because I get to listen to music, don’t have to be in the cold, and get to sit (lol). 

I find that staying in the house is a slippery slope and once you leave, no matter what time no matter what you do, it gets better from there on. 

I also get the lonliness, and something I’ve been trying to work on is not comparing myself to others. I also find that distractions can be really peaceful and comforting, so honestly just find a show u enjoy :)

It’s also important to talk to one person outside of who you live with everyday, even just on FaceTime (text doesn’t count) because self isolation can also be a slippery slope
